open_points.subject: Q29 re-grant and reassignment decision
open_points.text: Each accepted decision has one primary owner, the module that holds the decision's central mechanism, and consumers, except the two decisions recorded `cross_cutting` (A22, A26, below).
open_points.question: Which primary owner and consumers own the 2026-11-22 decision that revoked grants and assignments remain as history while a new active record may be created, and where must that decision be added to the ownership mapping?
options: Each identity use case (`viewer_access`, `staff_identity`, `service_identity`) owns re-creation and its repository owns only enforcement
Each corresponding repository owns the complete re-grant/reassignment rule
One named primary module owns the common rule and the three identity modules and repositories are consumers
open_points.default_guess: Make each identity use case the owner of its record's re-creation behavior and each corresponding repository a consumer responsible for the partial uniqueness constraint.

open_points.subject: active grant and assignment uniqueness
open_points.text: - INV-009: at most one active grant per (viewer_id, project_id) and per (service_principal_id, project_id)
open_points.question: Which accepted decision and owning module contain the equivalent at-most-one-active rule for `StaffProjectAssignment`, and does A8 still own the viewer and producer uniqueness rules after the Q29 change?
options: Extend A8 and its ownership mapping to all three active-record constraints
Place all three constraints under A3 and update its consumers
Create a new accepted decision for reusable active-grant uniqueness
open_points.default_guess: Create one explicit decision covering all three active-record constraints and map the three identity services and their repositories as consumers.

open_points.subject: ProjectViewerGrant persistence upgrade
open_points.text: One active grant per pair is now kept by a partial unique index (SPEC_STANDARD §6.3, tenth addition); the revoked records stay as history.
open_points.question: How is an existing SQLite viewer-grant table with a full UNIQUE `(viewer_id, project_id)` constraint upgraded so that re-granting after revocation actually works?
options: Rebuild and migrate the table, replacing the full constraint with a partial unique index
Introduce a new schema/table version and copy existing rows
Apply the partial index only to fresh databases and leave existing databases unchanged
open_points.default_guess: Use a transactional table rebuild that preserves rows and replaces the full unique constraint with a partial unique index on active rows.

witness.initial: A deployed database still has the old full UNIQUE constraint and contains a revoked viewer grant for viewer V and project P.
events: The deployment is upgraded to the new design.
An administrator grants V access to P again.
outcomes: A migration removed the old constraint, so a new active grant is inserted.
Only the new partial index was added, so the old full constraint rejects the insert and the administrator receives a failure.
witness.observer: The administrator attempting to restore the viewer's access

open_points.subject: StaffProjectAssignment persistence upgrade
open_points.text: One active assignment per pair is now kept by a partial unique index (SPEC_STANDARD §6.3, tenth addition); the revoked records stay as history.
open_points.question: How is an existing SQLite staff-assignment table with a full UNIQUE `(staff_id, project_id)` constraint upgraded to permit a new assignment after revocation?
options: Rebuild and migrate the table, replacing the full constraint with a partial unique index
Introduce a new schema/table version and copy existing rows
Apply the partial index only to fresh databases and leave existing databases unchanged
open_points.default_guess: Use a transactional table rebuild that preserves rows and replaces the full unique constraint with a partial unique index on active rows.

witness.initial: A deployed database has the old full UNIQUE constraint and a revoked assignment for staff member S and project P.
events: An administrator assigns S to P again.
outcomes: The old constraint was removed and a new active assignment is created.
The old constraint remains and rejects the new assignment.
witness.observer: The administrator and the operator whose access should be restored

open_points.subject: ProducerProjectGrant persistence upgrade
open_points.text: One active grant per pair is now kept by a partial unique index (SPEC_STANDARD §6.3, tenth addition); the revoked records stay as history.
open_points.question: How is an existing SQLite producer-grant table with a full UNIQUE `(service_principal_id, project_id)` constraint upgraded to permit a new grant after revocation?
options: Rebuild and migrate the table, replacing the full constraint with a partial unique index
Introduce a new schema/table version and copy existing rows
Apply the partial index only to fresh databases and leave existing databases unchanged
open_points.default_guess: Use a transactional table rebuild that preserves rows and replaces the full unique constraint with a partial unique index on active rows.

witness.initial: A deployed database has the old full UNIQUE constraint and a revoked grant for principal S and project P.
events: An administrator grants S access to P again.
outcomes: The old constraint was removed and the new active grant is inserted.
The old constraint remains and rejects the insert.
witness.observer: The administrator and the service principal attempting its next import

open_points.subject: revocation after a pair has been granted again
open_points.text: A revoked grant is terminal and no operation reactivates it; giving the pair access again creates a new grant record.
open_points.question: After a pair has historical revoked records and a new active record, do the viewer, staff-assignment and producer revocation operations identify the active record by pair or identify one exact record by `grant_id` or `assignment_id`, and what must happen to a stale repeated revocation request?
options: Commands identify the pair and always revoke its current active record
Commands identify the exact record id and cannot revoke a later replacement
Commands carry both pair and record id and reject a mismatch
open_points.default_guess: Identify the exact active record by id, verify its pair, and make a stale request leave a later replacement active.

witness.initial: Grant G1 for a pair was revoked and replacement grant G2 is active.
events: An administrator or delayed client repeats the revocation request originally intended for G1.
outcomes: Pair-based revocation resolves the current active row and revokes G2.
Record-based revocation finds G1 already revoked and leaves G2 active.
witness.observer: The principal whose replacement access either remains available or is unexpectedly removed

open_points.subject: simultaneous re-grant or reassignment
open_points.text: at most one active grant per `(viewer_id, project_id)`; revoked grants of the pair stay as history.
open_points.question: When two administrators concurrently create replacement active records for the same pair, what domain result must the losing operation return when the partial unique index rejects it?
options: Return the same typed active-duplicate refusal used when an active record was observed before insertion
Return the active record created by the winning operation as an idempotent result
Expose a persistence failure or HTTP 500
open_points.default_guess: Translate the constraint conflict into the operation's typed active-duplicate refusal and roll back all effects, including audit, from the losing operation.

witness.initial: A pair has only revoked historical records and therefore no active grant.
events: Administrator A and administrator B concurrently request access for the same pair.
Both operations reach creation before either has observed the other's committed active row.
outcomes: The loser receives a stable typed duplicate refusal and writes nothing.
The partial-index violation escapes as a persistence error or HTTP 500.
